$comment: What bounds a plugin call, its requests and its answers, taken from the device rather than chosen, the same on both hosts. callBudgetMs is the JS a call may run, summed over its runs (JsLimits.DEFAULT_CALL_TIMEOUT_MS). The wall-clock ceiling is callBudgetMs + requestTimeoutMs + ceilingMarginMs (JsLimits.wallClockCeilingMs). requestConnectTimeoutMs, requestReadTimeoutMs and requestTimeoutMs are one request's connect, idle-read and whole-request timeouts (NetworkModule, HttpTransport.CALL_TIMEOUT_MILLIS); CallLimitsRecordTest holds the device to them (kangzj/yonto#513). responseBodyBytes is the most of a response body yonto.fetch hands a plugin; a larger one is RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE (Jasper, 2026-09-23, kangzj/lantern-tv#333). unreadBodyBytesPerCall is the most of its bodies one call keeps for bodyBase64: past it the oldest is dropped, and its bodyBase64 reads as late. ResponseBodyLimitRecordTest holds the device's PluginHttpTransport.MAX_BODY_BYTES and MAX_UNREAD_BODY_BYTES to them. answerDepth is the deepest a call's answer may nest: one nested deeper is METHOD_THREW, read by neither host, since on iOS reading an answer 300 deep killed the app; PluginAnswerDepthRecordTest holds the device's JsRuntime.MAX_ANSWER_DEPTH to it. src/host/fetch.js, src/transport/live.js and src/engines/quickjs.js read them from here.
